sections.title: Performance Analysis — Canon Web
sections.content: Scope: `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `types/`, `drizzle/` (~30 files). This is an early-stage Next.js 16 app — everything except 4 leaf components is a Server Component, there's no client-side state (`useState`/`useEffect`/`useMemo` — zero hits across `app/` and `components/`), and there are no API routes yet. That changes what's actually *findable* here versus what a generic checklist would predict.

sections.title: 1. N+1 query patterns
2. Unnecessary React re-renders
sections.content: Nothing to fix here — worth saying explicitly rather than manufacturing a finding. There is no client-side state anywhere in the app (confirmed via grep for `useState`/`useEffect`/`useMemo`/`useCallback` — zero matches). The four `"use client"` components (`LandingHero`, `SourcesEmptyState`, `PipelineStrip`, presumably `GetStartedHero`) are pure animation wrappers around `motion/react` with no internal state, and `NavRail` (the only other client component) derives `active` from `usePathname()` over a 5-item, module-level `NAV` array — trivial, no memoization warranted. The `"use client"` boundaries are also correctly pushed to leaves rather than wrapping whole pages, which keeps the client bundle minimal. No action needed until actual client state (e.g., the run-status polling the comment in `sources.ts` mentions reserving TanStack Query for) shows up.

sections.title: 3. Caching opportunities
4. Memory leaks
sections.content: None found, and the app currently has no surface area for one: no `setInterval`/`setTimeout`, no `addEventListener`, no subscriptions, no `useEffect` at all. The one place a leak class commonly appears in Next.js dev — an unbounded Postgres pool being recreated on every hot reload — is already guarded against via the `globalForDb` caching pattern noted above.

sections.title: 5. Redundant computations
sections.content:
Same finding as #1: `countSourcesBySide()` doing a full select + full-row Zod validation + JS `.filter()` three times over, to produce three integers. That's the one concrete redundant-computation instance in the codebase today; the SQL `count(*) filter (...)` rewrite above eliminates both the redundant parsing and the redundant passes.

---
**Bottom line:** this codebase is too early-stage to have the bugs the prompt's checklist is built to catch (no client state, no loops of queries, no API routes). The one real issue — `countSourcesBySide`'s fetch-then-filter — and the two real opportunities — `cache()`-wrapping `listSources` and indexing the FK columns on `conflicts`/`resolutions`/`auditLog` before those pages exist — are worth doing now, cheaply, rather than after the `/runs` and `/conflicts` pages are built against an unindexed schema.
